name: Koneswarar Temple, Tirukkudavayil
deity: Shiva as Koneswarar, with the goddess Periyanayaki
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tirukkudavayil, now Kudavasal, midway between Kumbakonam and Tiruvarur, honours Shiva as Koneswarar with the goddess Periyanayaki. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar — the 94th shrine of the Kaveri's southern bank — it is one of the twelve temples bound to the origin of Kumbakonam, where the top of Brahma's sacred pot is said to have fallen in the great deluge.

sections.history: Tirukkudavayil, now called Kudavasal, lies almost midway between Kumbakonam (about 18 km) and Tiruvarur (about 20 km), in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, and counted the 94th shrine on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The temple is a maadakkovil attributed to Kochchenga Chola, its upper shrine entered from the south; the stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple raised in the maadakkovil form, the shrine enshrines Koneswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Periyanayaki in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. An 80-foot rajagopuram rises over the entrance, and the temple has two prakarams. The sacred tank is the Amirtatheertham.
sections.legends: Shiva is worshipped here as Koneswarar, with Periyanayaki, 'the great lady,' beside him. The place is one of the twelve temples tied to the origin of Kumbakonam and its Mahamaham: at the great deluge, when Brahma's sacred pot (kumbha) of nectar was borne upon the waters, its top is said to have fallen here, whence the name Kudavayil, 'the mouth of the pot.' The fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and Sambandar's verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes the Masi Magam Brahmotsavam in Masi (February–March), besides Maha Shivaratri, Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims of the Kumbakonam country, and those who keep the Mahamaham, include Tirukkudavayil among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tirukkudavayil the pilgrim comes to a shrine of the great deluge's memory. Before Koneswarar and Periyanayaki, under the tall rajagopuram midway between Kumbakonam and Tiruvarur, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple and the legend of the sacred pot whose top fell here.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirukkudavayil (Kudavasal) lies almost midway between Kumbakonam (about 18 km) and Tiruvarur (about 20 km), in Tiruvarur district. Kumbakonam and Tiruvarur are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to Kudavasal.
